messages:
maria: Heads-up — our preemptible GPU nodepool in eu-west2 started flapping after a big batch job ramped last night. Seeing lots of NotReady / NoSchedule from nodes during init.

maria: cc @ajay @kai, logs point at the NV plugin backoff loop + a TON of kubelet churn. Example from one node: 
```
Sep 22 03:04:02 k8s-gpu-spot-17 kubelet[1]: E0902 03:04:02 kernel: nvidia-device-plugin: Init failed: plugin startup throttled (rate_limit_exceeded)
Sep 22 03:04:03 k8s-gpu-spot-17 kubelet[1]: W0902 03:04:03 kubelet: NodeStatus not ready: device plugin unhealthy
Sep 22 03:04:05 k8s-gpu-spot-17 systemd[1]: containerd.service: Restarting too quickly
```

ajay: Oof. Any cloud-side spot eviction spikes? If many preemptible nodes are created at once the plugin might hammer metadata/API or a shared service.

maria: Provider metrics show a burst of new node attachments between 03:02–03:06 (autoscaler burst). No eviction spike prior — autoscaler opened a bunch to satisfy Pending GPU pods.

kai: Could be two things: 1) plugin starts N workers that race on a shared device file/socket causing EADDRINUSE / startup fails, or 2) a rate-limited call to fetch firmware/driver metadata (we saw this with older plugin versions). Which plugin version?

maria: Running nvidia-device-plugin v0.12.2 (we recently rolled). I see repeated 429s in the plugin logs to a local helper service: `GET /gpu-metadata` -> `429`.

ajay: That matches a startup-throttle pattern: helper service (gputooling) has a global limit of 200 req/min, when 50 nodes come up it trips and the plugin bails out and restarts. Workload: many model-server pods request GPUs with NodeSelector. Autoscaler bursts to fulfill, nodes never reach Ready.

oncall-sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-2154 — GPU pool initialization degraded in eu-west2. Pager off call assigned to @ajay.

kai: Short term: 1) add a 30s post-start sleep in the device plugin DaemonSet `preStop`/`postStart` hook to stagger initial bursts, or 2) tighten autoscaler burst params so we don't spin up dozens at once. Which is faster?

ajay: Staggering on the DaemonSet is fastest to push. I'll prepare a patch to the helm chart to add an init-sleep that reads `START_STAGGER_SEC` (default 0 -> set to 20s for preemptible pool).

maria: Also we should scale down the autoscaler `maxNodeProvisionRate` for the preemptible-gpu pool to 3 nodes/min so new capacity comes online gradually. That prevents hammering shared helper endpoints.

kai: Agreed. And add a retry/backoff improvement in the plugin: when local helper returns `429`, plugin should exponential backoff instead of immediate crashloop. I'll open a PR to the plugin repo.

ajay: Patch rolled to cluster (helm chart): added `START_STAGGER_SEC=20` as env in DaemonSet and bumped readinessProbe initialDelay to 45s for that pool. Deploying to eu-west2 now.

maria: Deploy looks good so far. Monitoring shows fewer 429s and a steady ramp of Ready nodes instead of a pile of NotReady.

ajay: Autoscaler param change: `maxNodeProvisionRate: 3` applied to preemptible-gpu node group with immediate effect. We'll watch cost/latency (some pending pods slightly slower to schedule).

kai: PR link to plugin backoff improvement: https://git.internal/redwood/nv-plugin/pull/428 (adds Jittered exponential backoff on metadata calls).

maria: Follow-ups: 
- ajay: confirm no user-facing outage (SLOs) and close INC if stable.
- kai: merge plugin PR and cut new image (v0.12.3) then roll next week.
- infra: consider making helper service cluster-local per-AZ to reduce global throttling.

ajay: Ack. Posting quick postmortem note in #incidents after 2 hours of stable Ready counts. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Incident INC-2024-2154 status -> monitoring (stability improving).

maria: Thanks team. Leaving the thread open for another hour; ping me if anything regresses.
